messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: CONFIG-MONITOR alert — SecurityGroup sg-0a1b2c3d now allows 0.0.0.0/0 on tcp/22 and tcp/5432. Detected 2026-03-20T14:12:01Z. link: https://console.aws/alerts/CONFIG/abc123

alex: seeing this. oncall? @jordan

jordan: oncall here, I'll take it. suspending any change windows and isolating now.

jordan: revoking ingress rules (running):
```
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d --protocol tcp --port 22 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d --protocol tcp --port 5432 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
```

jordan: exec done, returns OK. verifying with describe: `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0a1b2c3d` shows no 0.0.0.0/0 for those ports.

maria: good. can we confirm whether there were any active inbound connections while the rule was present? please check VPC Flow Logs and instance netstat.

jordan: querying VPC Flow Logs (quick filter) — saw 4 src IPs connect to 22/5432 between 14:08-14:11Z: 35.201.12.7, 54.93.45.2, 3.120.88.10, 18.204.3.5. All are external.

maria: check CloudTrail for AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress events around 14:05-14:10Z. also check principal that performed the change.

leah: pulling CloudTrail... event: AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress, time 2026-03-20T14:05:42Z, userIdentity: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-runner-role, sourceIP: 18.204.3.5, requestParameters show cidr 0.0.0.0/0, ports 22,5432.

alex: looks like a CI job applied a test infra change and didn't remove it. why did CI have permission to modify prod SGs?

leah: that pipeline was supposed to target a test SG but a variable mismatch pointed it at sg-0a1b2c3d (prod). investigating why the env var was wrong. job name: infra-e2e-456.

maria: we need to see if any secrets were accessed. check KMS decrypt logs for the CI role around that time (kms:Decrypt) and S3 GetObject for artifacts. if KMS decrypts from that role are non-zero -> escalate.

jordan: ran quick KMS query: no Decrypt events from that principal in the last 24h besides CI role using ephemeral creds to pull job artifacts at 14:02Z — those are expected. S3 access logs show artifact GETs from our artifact-bucket (encrypted with aws/kms key alias/redwood-artifacts).

alex: ok no signs of data exfil via KMS. we still need containment and follow-ups: 1) confirm rule removed (done), 2) revoke CI role's temporary token and rotate any deploy creds used in that job, 3) create postmortem and fix IaC guardrails.

leah: I've revoked the specific session (sts:RevokeSession simulated) and kicked off rotation for the short-lived creds used by that pipeline. opening ticket SEC-2026-457 for cred rotation + pipeline fix.

maria: follow-ups to add to ticket: - deny wide-cidr for ports 22/5432 in org SCP or guardrail, - add CI pipeline sanity check to assert target SG id whitelist, - create alert for AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress when principal matches ci-runner-role, - enable more granular KMS audit if not already.

jordan: also recommend enabling real-time VPC Flow Log alerting for unusual inbound from public internet to DB ports.

alex: can infra patch terraform module to prevent accidental apply to prod SGs (use workspace check)? also add a preflight in PR checks.

leah: yes I will push a hotfix: repo infra/security-groups -> add validation, update pipeline variables, and add deny rule in sentinel/policy as fallback. PR coming in ~30m.

maria: I'll draft a short incident blurb for #incidents and notify product/security leadership. note: no confirmed data access or key misuse. containment status: resolved (ingress revoked).

alex: thanks team. assign owners in SEC-2026-457: leah (pipeline + IaC fix), maria (audit + comms), jordan (forensic + flow log alert). leaving this thread open until postmortem is attached to the ticket. :thumbsup:
